name: The papers as a discerning trust attorney, trust officer and executor read them
summary: I rendered every paper the desk produces on five estates and saved them: the Ashworth probate with a co-PR, a 706 estate with MAIV, appraisals, sales, a statement, receipts, an incident and keys; a trust with a co-trustee, named and valued through the real Name 24 shots press; a contents-tier probate; a 300-line probate; and the living Hale move. I also pressed the dashboard's Send probate package and Send trust package and read the drafts. The schedules are carefully honest about gaps. A floor is called a floor, DRAFT names its reasons and the fix, and a signature block is withheld while a line is unvalued. The release request letter is the strongest paper: item numbers, photographs, initials by value and destination, a ratification section, a signature line for each fiduciary, and a firearms block with serial and dealer. They stop short of what a Palm Beach trusts-and-estates lawyer or a bank trust officer would rely on, in six ways. (1) The Estate Inventory Report, which goes in every package, prints "Total estimated fair market value" with unvalued lines counted as $0 and non-probate property summed in, and it calls exempt property "carved out of the probate estate". The Court Inventory attached beside it says the opposite and shows a different total. (2) The schedules carry no item number, room or photo reference, so their lines cannot be matched to the photographs, receipts or ledger. (3) On a full house only about 110 lines get a photograph on any paper, and the page tells counsel to "re-open this tab". (4) The evidence behind a value never leaves the app: comparables, range, confidence, marks read, and who reviewed it. A figure the TC types prints "not stated" in red. (5) A §733.604 or Chapter 736 schedule prints FINAL with a signature block while every value on it is an unreviewed agent estimate. (6) Nothing flags a fiduciary receiving or buying estate property, or a release that went without written approval, on the ledger the PR signs as "the final record". The living papers are in better shape. But the Appraisal Worklist tells a living client's appraiser to value "as of date of death". A best-in-class package would add a cover summary, a methodology and evidence appendix, per-line value bases, and linked photographs. I offer the wording for each only as a question for Anthony and counsel.
works_well: The Court Inventory and Trust Schedule refuse to conclude while a line is unvalued: 'Total recorded so far — not a complete total', the unvalued lines named by number, DRAFT with each reason and its own fix, and the signature block withheld (audit/DOC/out/ash_Court_Inventory.html, trust_trust.html).
A schedule that is the wrong instrument says so on its own face: the Court Inventory on a trust matter, the Trust Schedule on a probate matter.

The release approval request letter: a Dear line naming every fiduciary, item numbers and photographs, an own initial at $500 and up, one initial per destination group, an 'Already released: for ratification' section, a signature line for each fiduciary, and the firearms block with serial and dealer (out/ash_Havellin_Release_Approval_Request_*.html, hale_*Request*.html).
The Disposition Ledger checks proceeds against the vendor's statement ('Agrees'), links the filed receipt per line, and withholds its sign-off while any line is undecided.
The Key and Access record and the ledger's embedded copy never print the code digits ('held').

The Appraisal Worklist works through the §20.2031-6(b) MAIV aggregate by class, refusing to call an untested total a total, and lists grouped lots with their per-article arithmetic under §20.2031-6(a).

Send probate package is one press plus one confirm that names the gaps. It builds five PDFs, files them, shares both photograph folders, and drafts to the attorney with the PR, the co-PR and agreements@ copied. It is refused before activation.
A scan of every saved paper found no raw ISO dates, no 'agent' or 'unsure', no 'undefined' and no NaN. The CSV is the exception.
Every paper fits Letter. No table runs wider than the page in print emulation (a5.js), and the More ▾ papers open in the viewer first.
The Donation Record and the beneficiary receipt carry careful limits: no claim of value or ownership, and the deduction left to the donor's adviser.
measurements: Ashworth package (a2.js, then a5.js page.pdf on Letter with 0.5 in margins) for 16 lines: Court Inventory 2 pages, Estate Inventory Report 4, Disposition Ledger 2, Incident Record 1, Appraisal Worklist 1; no table wider than the page.

300-line probate (a6.js), built on the page: Court Inventory 9 Letter pages (built in 9 ms), Estate Inventory Report 28 pages (8 ms, 382 KB of html, 509 KB with the app CSS sent to htmlToPdf), ledger 1 page (1 ms). About 56 pages of Report for a 600-line house.

Photographs on the papers, 300-line estate with getThumbnails answering every file at 18 KB (a7.js): 306 asked, 110 held in the cache (localStorage 1,984,071 chars against the 2,000,000 cap), 110 on the Estate Inventory Report, and the text '190 items have no photograph available on this device … re-open this tab'. After leaving and reopening the desk: still 110.

Same estate, two totals in one package (a1/a2): Court Inventory 'Total recorded so far — not a complete total: $18,635' (4 unvalued). Estate Inventory Report 'Total estimated fair market value: $32,635', with no floor note (the same 4 unvalued plus the $14,000 non-probate car).

Unreviewed agent values against status: Court Inventory 'FINAL · 300 values not yet reviewed' with 'Reviewed and adopted by' for the PR (a6, out/big_court.pdf). Trust Schedule 'FINAL · 24 values not yet reviewed' with both trustees' receipt lines, once the two nothing-to-list lines were removed (a8.js).
Cost of clearing the nothing-to-list rows that hold a schedule at DRAFT (a8.js): tick 2 rows, press Remove lines, accept 1 confirm.
Package presses (a2.js, a4.js): 1 press of Send probate package or Send trust package plus 1 confirm, then 5 (probate) or 4 (trust) PDFs attached.
verifier_note: The DOC report holds up well. I reproduced every behavioural claim with my own scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/DOC-verify/ (v1.js Ashworth probate, v1b.js every line decided plus Hale, v2.js a trust with a co-trustee named and valued through the real Name 24 shots press, v3.js a 300-line probate with thumbnails). The fixtures are the step 99 seed or seedFullHouse, plus a few line fields that real desk controls set (Exempt tick, Asset Track, Date of Disposition, a disposition). Figures were typed into the real Total boxes. Two proposals run into Anthony's recorded rules and are DECIDED_CONFLICT: DOC-04 (an unreviewed agent figure counts as valued and withholds nothing) and DOC-09 (a typed figure reads 'not stated' until the desk names a source). Severities changed: DOC-02 from fix-now to high (the filed Court Inventory is right); DOC-06, DOC-14 and DOC-24 down; DOC-17, DOC-20 and DOC-28 to low. One figure did not reproduce: DOC-24's page count. The 300-line Report ran 19 Letter pages here, not 28; it depends on how many disposition groups and rooms there are. DOC-23 and part of DOC-16 rest on expert judgement about what counsel expects. I confirmed today's behaviour for both; the legal call stays with counsel.

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 (P7, its critical part: CLAUDE.md, a floor is a floor on every valued paper; tests/p7-evidence.test.js, browser step 122)
findings.title: Estate Inventory Report prints a 'total' that silently counts unvalued lines as $0 and mixes in non-probate property
findings.where: Estate Inventory PDF (work bar, and in every probate or trust package): printEstateInventoryReport, totalFMV at havellin.html:31137, the total row at about 31147
findings.evidence: a1.js and a2.js on Ashworth 9601. The Report reads 'Total estimated fair market value: $32,635' with 4 lines unvalued (#20, #23, #26, #42) and no caveat. The Court Inventory in the same package reads 'Total recorded so far … not a complete total: $18,635' and names the 4 lines. The $14,000 gap is the Non-probate car, which the Report sums into its total. Trust 9700 (a4.js): Report 'Total estimated fair market value: $9,340' while the Trust Schedule calls $9,340 a floor (#8 and #20 unvalued). Code: totalFMV = all.reduce(... isNaN ? 0 ...), with no unvalued test.
findings.tc_impact: Counsel receives two attachments with two different totals for one estate. The Report's figure reads as complete when it is a floor, and on a probate it includes property that passes outside the estate. A trust officer reconciling the two finds the discrepancy before Havellin does.
findings.proposal: Apply the Court Inventory's floor rule to the Report: 'Total recorded so far — not a complete total', with the unvalued lines named by number, whenever any line lacks a value. On a probate matter print a subtotal for the probate estate (exempt included), a subtotal for property outside it, then the grand total, each labelled. One helper, shared by printEstateInventoryReport and printCourtInventory, so the two cannot disagree. No new TC press.
findings.vnote: Ashworth with three lines unvalued (#20, #23, #26) and a Non-probate Mercedes at $14,000. The Court Inventory reads 'Total recorded so far (Fair Market Value) — not a complete total: $14,475' and names the three. The Estate Inventory Report in the same package reads 'Total estimated fair market value: $28,475' ($14,475 plus the carved-out car) with no floor note. The Domain rule says a schedule with an unvalued line reports a floor; the Report breaks it. Code: totalFMV at havellin.html:31139 counts NaN as 0 and sums every line, carved ones included.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('== DOC-01 totals'); papers saved as DOC-verify/out/ash_court.html, ash_report.html; havellin.html:31139

findings.title: Exempt property is 'carved out of the probate estate' on the Report but 'listed and claimed' on the Court Inventory
findings.where: printEstateInventoryReport: carved = _invIsExempt || !_invIsProbateAsset (about havellin.html:31033), heading 'Property — carved out of the probate estate' (31145). Contrast printCourtInventory footnote 'Exempt property is not excluded — it is listed above and claimed under §732.402'. Also manual.html's Estate Inventory PDF paragraph.
findings.evidence: a1.js on Ashworth: the sofa (#43, flagExempt) sits under 'Exempt, Non-probate Property — carved out of the probate estate' on the Report, and under 'Exempt Property (Fla. Stat. §732.402)' inside the probate schedule on the Court Inventory, with 'Exempt property is not excluded'. The code comment above _invIsExempt says exempt 'IS A CLAIM AGAINST THE PROBATE ESTATE, NOT A POT OUTSIDE IT'. The manual describes the Report's carve-out as showing property that 'sits outside the probate estate'.
findings.tc_impact: The same item gets two legal characterisations in one package sent to the estate attorney, and the Report's version is the one the app's own rule calls wrong. That is embarrassing in front of counsel, and it understates the probate estate on the Report.
findings.proposal: On the Report, keep exempt lines inside the Asset Schedule under their own 'Exempt property claimed (§732.402)' subsection with a subtotal. Carve out only Trust, Non-probate and Homestead, using _invOnProbateSchedule as the Court Inventory does. Update the manual's sentence. Ask Anthony and counsel to confirm the heading's words.
findings.vnote: I ticked the sofa Exempt. The Report puts it under 'Exempt, Non-probate Property — carved out of the probate estate'. The Court Inventory lists it under 'Exempt Property (Fla. Stat. §732.402)' and says 'Exempt property is not excluded — it is listed above and claimed under §732.402'. The Report's filter (carved = _invIsExempt || !_invIsProbateAsset, havellin.html:31034) contradicts the app's own rule at 28286 ('EXEMPT IS A CLAIM AGAINST THE PROBATE ESTATE, NOT A POT OUTSIDE IT'). MANUAL.md:2336 and manual.html:2410 describe the carve-out as property that 'sits outside the probate estate'. Rated high, not fix-now, because the instrument actually filed (the Court Inventory) is right.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('== DOC-02 exempt', 'REPORT sofa under carved? true'); havellin.html:31034, 31145; MANUAL.md:2336

findings.title: On a full house only about 110 lines get a photograph on any paper, and the page tells counsel to 're-open this tab'
findings.where: _invPrintThumb (about havellin.html:30683), read by the Estate Inventory Report, Contents List, Contents Record and Release Approval Request. The thumbnail cache is capped by INV_THUMB_CACHE_MAX = 2,000,000 (28521) with oldest-first eviction (_invSaveThumbCache), and _invThumbTried (28585) stops an evicted id being fetched again. The 're-open this tab with a connection' sentence is printed by printContentsList (30996) and printEstateInventoryReport.
findings.evidence: a7.js: a 300-line estate, with getThumbnails answering 18 KB per file. 306 requested; the cache kept 110 (1,984,071 chars); the Report carried 110 and printed '190 items have no photograph available on this device … re-open this tab with a connection to include them'. Leaving and reopening the desk: still 110. sendProbatePackage builds the PDFs without fetching thumbnails first.
findings.tc_impact: For roughly two-thirds of a 300-line house, the attorney, executor or trust officer gets a glyph where the photograph should be, on the Report and on the request the fiduciaries initial. The TC cannot fix it by reopening the tab, and the paper asks a reader who has no tab to open one.
findings.proposal: Have the printers fetch thumbnails for exactly the lines on the page into a print-only map in memory, never localStorage, before building. The package already waits on refreshPhotoRefs; add a thumbnail pass with a progress step, 'Gathering N photographs…'. Wrap every line's photograph in a link to its driveFileUrl. Replace the 're-open this tab' sentence on client papers with a count the desk shows only to the TC. Functions: _invPrintThumb, sendProbatePackage, printEstateInventoryReport, printContentsList, printApprovalRequest, printContentsRecord.
findings.vnote: A 300-line probate, with getThumbnails answering 18 KB per file. The server was asked for 306 thumbnails in 6 batches. The cache kept 110 (1,984,071 chars against INV_THUMB_CACHE_MAX 2,000,000). The Report carried 110 and printed '190 items have no photograph available on this device … re-open this tab with a connection to include them'. After leaving and reopening the desk: cache 110, 110 , no new requests. Cause: _invSaveThumbCache evicts from the in-memory cache object itself (havellin.html:28525-28530), and _invThumbTried (28585) blocks a second fetch for the rest of the session. The cache also spends budget on as-found and detail shots.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v3.js -> v3.out (lines 1-4); havellin.html:28521-28541, 28573, 28585

findings.title: A §733.604 or Chapter 736 schedule prints FINAL, with its adoption or receipt signature block, while every value on it is an unreviewed agent estimate
findings.where: printCourtInventory status (havellin.html:34113) and printTrustSchedule: _avUnreviewedStamp (39328) only adds a badge beside FINAL
findings.evidence: a6.js on a 300-line probate: Court Inventory 'FINAL · 300 values not yet reviewed', total $117,240, then 'Reviewed and adopted by: ____ Daniel Price · Personal Representative' (out/big_court.pdf). a8.js on trust 9700, after Remove lines took off two nothing-to-list rows: Trust Schedule 'FINAL · 24 values not yet reviewed' with 'Received for the trust's records by' lines for both trustees.
findings.tc_impact: Nobody at Havellin has to look at a single figure before a personal representative adopts the schedule or a trustee receives it. If a value is wrong, the verified inventory carries it under the fiduciary's signature. Outcompeting a 20-year appraiser requires that a FINAL page means a person stood behind it.
findings.proposal: Keep the decided rule that an unreviewed agent figure counts toward totals and nothing is hidden. But let 'N values not yet reviewed' be a DRAFT reason that withholds only the signature block, saying 'a final copy follows once Havellin has reviewed each value'. The TC clears it with the line's existing one tick, so no new press. If Anthony keeps FINAL, at least mark each unreviewed line (DOC-05).
findings.decided_conflict: Domain rules, Agent Two's figures: 'An unreviewed agent figure counts as valued; the Court Inventory, the Trust Schedule and the Estate Inventory PDF print _avUnreviewedStamp beside their status' (Anthony, 2026-10-06, spec §12.2: nothing is withheld for it).
findings.vnote: Behaviour confirmed: trust 9700 after the real Name 24 shots press, with the two nothing-to-list lines removed through the pick boxes and Remove lines. The Trust Schedule reads 'FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed', then receipt lines for Daniel Price and Ruth Price. The proposal (make unreviewed values a DRAFT reason that withholds the signature block) runs against the Domain rule under Agent Two's figures: 'An unreviewed agent figure counts as valued; the Court Inventory, the Trust Schedule and the Estate Inventory PDF print _avUnreviewedStamp beside their status' (Anthony, 2026-10-06, spec §12.2: nothing is withheld for it). It also sits beside the Decided item against 'A second review of Agent Two's figures'. The case for revisiting is strong, but it is Anthony's call.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v2.js -> v2.out; DOC-verify/out/trust_schedule_after.html ('FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed'); havellin.html:39328

findings.title: The valued schedules give no item number, room or photograph per line, so a reader cannot cross-reference or tell two like items apart
findings.where: _invScheduleSection (havellin.html:33978), shared by the Court Inventory and the Trust Schedule. Columns are Description · Condition · Basis · FMV only, with auto table layout per category. The claim 'Item numbers are the ones every inventory document cites' is printed by probatePackageRecordHtml (17840), the beneficiary receipt (33406) and 31732.
findings.evidence: a1.js on the Ashworth Court Inventory: no '#' on any row. Numbers appear only in the floor note ('#42 Diamond solitaire ring…'). The unnamed #26 prints as a row of dashes. a4.js on the trust: the Trust Schedule lists 'Remington 870 pump shotgun $500' twice and 'Oil on canvas harbor scene… $1,200' twice, and nothing on the page says whether that is two items or one double count. In the Court Inventory PNG (out/court-1.png) the columns shift position from one category table to the next.
findings.tc_impact: The paper the PR adopts cannot be matched to the photograph, the appraisal, the receipt or the ledger. Counsel has to cross-walk it by hand against the Report. A double count cannot be seen on the instrument that is filed.
findings.proposal: Add Item # and Room columns to _invScheduleSection. Sort by item number within each category. Use table-layout:fixed with one set of column widths so every category aligns. Optionally add a small 'photo' link to driveFileUrl, as the Appraisal Worklist already does. Mark unreviewed agent figures and pending appraisals per line with a footnote marker; this needs no change to the decided rule. No TC press.
findings.vnote: The Court Inventory's table headers are 'Description | Condition | Basis | FMV (total)', with no item number or room on any row (_invScheduleSection, havellin.html:33978). On the trust's Trust Schedule, 'Remington 870 pump shotgun Good general estimate $500' prints twice (two lines, #11 and #23), and nothing on the page tells them apart from a double count. Three other papers say 'Item numbers are the ones every inventory document cites' (havellin.html:17840, 31732, 33406), which the two schedules do not.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('COURT headers'); DOC-verify/out/trust_schedule_after.html (shotgun twice); havellin.html:33978-34000

findings.title: 'Photographs are reference-numbered to the line items above' is false: file names carry room and sequence, and no line links to its file
findings.where: Footer of printEstateInventoryReport (about havellin.html:31180) and printContentsList (31000). File names come from _captureShot: hvlId_Room_INV_seq_stamp.jpg (about 40674), where seq is per room and the item number is issued later at the desk.
findings.evidence: Code: var filename = hvlId + cleanRoom + '_' + tag + '_' + seq + '_' + _photoStamp(ts) + '.jpg'. The item number (#7) is assigned by _invAssignItemNos and never enters the file name. The Report's photo cell is an inline thumbnail with no href (itemRow). Only the CSV's Photo Link column, and the Worklist's 'photo', link per line.
findings.tc_impact: Counsel opening the shared 'Estate Inventory photographs' folder sees LivingRoom_INV_3 and cannot find #7 Grandfather clock in it. The paper promises a correspondence the app never made, which breaks 'never print a claim the app did not witness'.
findings.proposal: Make each line's photograph cell a link to its Drive file (and its close-ups) on the Report, the Contents List and the Contents Record. Either print the file name under the item number, or reword the footer to what is true ('each photograph is linked from its line'), as a question for Anthony. Functions: itemRow in printEstateInventoryReport, printContentsList, _invPrintThumb.
findings.vnote: The saved Report has 0 <a href> and no Drive link on any line. Its footer reads 'Photographs are reference-numbered to the line items above and retained for seven years.' Photo file names are hvlId_Room_INV_seq_stamp.jpg, where seq counts within the room and the item number is issued later (havellin.html:40664, 40675). The code comment at 31010 quotes the website's §02 promise, 'reference-numbered and linked to the corresponding line'. Rated medium, not high: the workbook and CSV do carry a Photo Link per line, so counsel can map a line to its photograph there, though not from the PDF.
findings.vrepro: grep on DOC-verify/out/ash_report.html, trust_report.html (0 links); havellin.html:31163, 31000, 40675

findings.title: The Appraisal Worklist tells the appraiser 'value as of date of death' on a living client's job, and ignores the alternate valuation date
findings.where: printAppraisalWorklist header, havellin.html:35375 ('Items flagged for specialist appraisal · value as of date of death' + dod). It never reads job.avd or estateValueDate.
findings.evidence: a3.js on Hale 9602 (Robert Hale, living Home Transition), the worklist from More ▾: 'Robert Hale · HVL-2610-T961 Items flagged for specialist appraisal · value as of date of death · October 26, 2026' (out/hale_Appraisal_Worklist.html). Every other desk paper goes through _invDocHead or estateValueDate, which follow the AVD.
findings.tc_impact: The appraiser Havellin hands this page to on a living move is told the client has died. On an estate that elected the §2032 alternate date, the appraiser is told the wrong valuation date.
findings.proposal: On an estate, build the line from estateValueDate(job), labelled 'the alternate valuation date' when job.avd is set, as _invDocHead does. On living work state no death and no valuation date, or ask Anthony for the words (for example 'current fair market value').
findings.vnote: Hale (living Home Transition): More ▾ offers 'Appraisal Worklist'. Its page reads 'Robert Hale · HVL-2610-T961 Items flagged for specialist appraisal · value as of date of death · October 26, 2026'. The date shown is the print date, so it reads as the date of death. The header is a fixed string at havellin.html:35375 and never reads job.avd or estateValueDate. _invDocHead and printCourtInventory both read job.avd. It is wrong valuation wording on the page given to a living client's appraiser.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('Hale More menu items', 'HALE worklist head'); DOC-verify/out/hale_worklist.html; havellin.html:35374-35375

findings.title: The evidence behind a value never leaves the app: no comparables, range, confidence or reviewer on any paper, CSV or workbook
findings.where: valComps is read only by _avComp, _avPanelHtml (the desk record), _avWrite and agentValueUseSale. valLow, valHigh, valConf, valReviewedBy and valuedBy reach no printer. INVENTORY_COLUMNS and _invExportValue carry valNote as 'Valuation Basis / Comps', but never the comps.
findings.evidence: grep of valComps across havellin.html: functions _avComp (38611), _avPanelHtml (39280), _avWrite (38646), agentValueUseSale (39097), savePhotoRefs. No paper is among them. a1/a2: the Rolex reads only 'Auction comps $5,200' on the Court Inventory, Report and CSV, while the desk holds its comparables, its $4,500 to $6,000 range and 'medium' confidence. The dresser's sold comparable (LiveAuctioneers, $425) appears on no paper.
findings.tc_impact: When counsel, a beneficiary or the IRS asks 'why $5,200?', the TC has to open the desk and rebuild the answer. The differentiator Anthony wants (research a spreadsheet appraiser cannot match) is invisible to the person paying for it.
findings.proposal: Add a 'Valuation evidence' appendix to the Estate Inventory Report, and optionally the package, one entry per researched line by item number: each comparable kept (title, sale date, price, link), the range, and who reviewed the figure and when. Add 'Comparables' and 'Reviewed by' columns to INVENTORY_COLUMNS for the workbook and CSV. Build it from the fields _avWrite already writes; the TC does nothing new.
findings.vnote: valComps is read only by _avComp/AGENT_VALUE_OWN (38611), _avWrite (38646), agentValueUseSale (39097), _avPanelHtml (39280) and the save whitelist (27542). No printer and no INVENTORY_COLUMNS entry reads it. valLow, valHigh, valConf and valReviewedBy likewise reach no paper. In v1 the Rolex's comparables and its $4,500 to $6,000 range appeared on no saved paper. The proposal fits the decided rules: it builds from fields already written and adds no review step.
findings.vrepro: grep -n valComps havellin.html (27542, 38611, 38646, 39097, 39280); DOC-verify/out/ash_court.html, ash_report.html, ash.csv

findings.title: A figure the TC types prints 'not stated' in red on the court schedule, and the source list has no choice for Havellin's own estimate
findings.where: _avTakeValue (about havellin.html:38760-38770) deletes an agent source when a figure is typed. INV_VAL_SOURCES (28235) offers Appraisal, Auction comps, Dealer quote, General estimate, Online comps, PR estimate and WorthPoint comps. _invScheduleSection and the Report print 'not stated' in red where there is no source. A living job has no source box at all.
findings.evidence: a10.js on Ashworth: I typed $4,800 into #46's real Total box (input[onchange*="_invEdit(9601,'e46','fmv'"]) and pressed Tab. The record became {fmv: 4800, src: '', by: 'desk'}. The Court Inventory row now reads 'Rolex Datejust wristwatch … not stated $4,800' and the Report row '$4,800 not stated'. The stand mixer ($120, typed) reads 'not stated' on every Ashworth paper.
findings.tc_impact: Every correction the TC makes costs a second pick in a record dropdown, and no choice in it is honest for the TC's own judgment ('General estimate' is the agent's, 'PR estimate' is the representative's). Otherwise a red 'not stated' lands on the attorney's schedule, on a tier whose contract promises 'the basis of each value stated'.
findings.proposal: When a person types a figure, record valSource as a new source such as 'Havellin estimate', with valuedBy 'desk' and the person's name already stamped, and print it as 'Havellin estimate · Ashley Jerome'. Add the source to INV_VAL_SOURCES and INV_VAL_BASIS_WORDS. Ask Anthony for the word. This removes a press per correction and the red text.
findings.vnote: Behaviour confirmed through the real Total box: typing $4,800 over the Rolex's Agent Two figure (Auction comps) left src='' and by='desk'. The Court Inventory then reads 'Rolex … as photographed not stated $4,800' and the Report '$4,800 not stated'. INV_VAL_SOURCES has no Havellin-own source, and valSource is an estate-only column (fid:true). This is the Domain rule as written under Agent Two's figures: 'a figure the desk types over the agent's drops the agent's source (AGENT_VALUE_SOURCES) and sentence, so the line reads *not stated* until the desk names one' (job-flow audit). Stamping a new source automatically would revise that rule. It is a sound case, so put it to Anthony.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('v46 fmv=4800 src= by=desk', '== DOC-09'); havellin.html:38766-38770, 28235, 28412

findings.title: Nothing flags a fiduciary receiving or buying estate or trust property
findings.where: INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS (havellin.html:32108 onward) holds flagBequest, flagDisputed, bequestElsewhere, staffRecipient (living), flaggedUnvalued (living) and needsAppraisal. None tests whether the recipient is in jobFiduciaries(job). Read by printApprovalRequest, the ledger and the row chips.
findings.evidence: a4.js on trust 9700: #3 White porcelain dinner plates, Distribute to Ruth Price, who is the recorded Co-Trustee. The request lists it with only 'Initial once for the item above going to Ruth Price (Distribute)' and no caution, and she is one of the two people approving her own distribution. a1.js on Ashworth: #44 Mercedes $14,000 to Nora Ashworth (Co-PR), no caution on the request or the ledger.
findings.tc_impact: Self-dealing by a fiduciary is the classic estate dispute: a sale to the PR can be voided, and trustees owe a duty of loyalty. The papers Havellin produces would show it with no flag, and a beneficiary's counsel would ask why Havellin's own record did not note it.
findings.proposal: As a question for Anthony and counsel: add a caution 'fiduciaryRecipient' (estate and trust; a flag, never a refusal) where a release or sale names one of jobFiduciaries by samePerson. Badge the line on the request and the ledger ('TO A FIDUCIARY'), require the line's own initial from each other fiduciary, and name it in the request's cautions. Functions: INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS, invReleaseCautions, invOwnInitial.
findings.vnote: INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS (havellin.html:32111-32235) holds flagBequest, flagDisputed, bequestElsewhere, staffRecipient (living), flaggedUnvalued (living) and needsAppraisal. None of them tests jobFiduciaries. On Ashworth the request lists '#44 2014 Mercedes-Benz E350 sedan … $14,000 Distribute Nora Ashworth', and Nora is the recorded Co-Personal Representative; the line carries no badge and no caution. Rated medium, because a distribution to a fiduciary who is also a beneficiary is routine. The real exposure is a sale or purchase. Any flag should be a flag, never a refusal, worded with counsel.
findings.vrepro: DOC-verify/v1.js -> v1.out ('REQUEST mercedes'); DOC-verify/out/ash_request.html; havellin.html:32111-32235

findings.title: Every value on a fiduciary's paper is unmarked as reviewed or not, so 'N values not yet reviewed' names no lines

A per-line mark on a printed paper does not contradict the decided 'one review' rule: no desk tier or badge is added. Rated medium: the stamp already tells the reader that unreviewed figures exist.

findings.title: The package goes out with no cover summary of what is open, and without the As-Found index
findings.where: sendProbatePackage (havellin.html:18044), buildProbatePackageEmailText and Html, and probatePackageDocs (no 'asfound' page)

findings.title: No valuation methodology, standard definition or preparer statement on the valued papers
findings.where: printCourtInventory, printTrustSchedule and printEstateInventoryReport footers ('Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death'; 'Prepared by Havellin Palm Beach, LLC')
findings.evidence: Every valued paper captured (out/ash_Court_Inventory.html, ash_Havellin_Estate_Inventory_*.html, trust_trust.html) states the basis and date. None defines fair market value, says how the figures were reached (how many appraised and by whom with credential, how many researched against sold comparables, how many general going-rate estimates, how many Havellin estimates), names the person who reviewed them, or states limiting conditions. Appraised values are also called 'estimated'.
findings.tc_impact: A Palm Beach attorney or bank trust officer judges defensibility by method and who stands behind it. A twenty-year appraiser's report carries both; this package carries neither.
findings.proposal: As a question for Anthony and counsel (wording is theirs): a generated 'How these values were reached' page on the Report and in the package, with counts by INV_VAL_SOURCES, the appraisers and credentials (_apprLabel), the reviewers (valReviewedBy), the standard and date, and a short limiting-conditions paragraph. Built from fields already on the lines, with no TC work.
findings.vnote: Today's footers are as described. The Court Inventory: 'Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death.' The Report: 'Total estimated fair market value'. Neither has a definition, a methodology, counts by source, a reviewer or limiting conditions. Appraised figures fall under the same 'estimated' sentence. What a Palm Beach attorney expects is expert judgement I cannot test here. The proposal is offered as a question for Anthony and counsel and conflicts with no decided rule.
findings.vrepro: grep on DOC-verify/out/ash_court.html ('Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death.'); havellin.html:34203, 31141

findings.evidence: a9.js on the Ashworth ledger: 'IN PROGRESS — 12 of 16 items reviewed … Values and dispositions on unreviewed lines may still change … This ledger is not yet complete. 4 lines sold … no proceeds recorded', then 'Reviewed and approved as the final record of the disposition' with both PRs' lines. The Hale Contents Record: 'IN PROGRESS — 3 of 6 items reviewed', then 'Signature: ____ Robert Hale, Client'.
findings.tc_impact: A family or fiduciary is asked to sign 'the final record' on a page that says it is a working copy. The TC must remember to reprint later, and the filed signed copy may be the provisional one.
findings.proposal: Ask Anthony: either withhold the sign-off while the stamp reads IN PROGRESS, or word the block for the state it is in ('approved as the record to date'). The Contents Record's stamp should take the noValues wording, since it states no values.
findings.vnote: Every Ashworth line decided. The ledger prints 'IN PROGRESS — 5 of 9 items reviewed … Values and dispositions on unreviewed lines may still change', then 'This ledger is not yet complete. 3 lines sold … with no proceeds recorded yet …', then 'Reviewed and approved as the final record of the disposition of the property listed above' with both PRs' lines. Hale's Contents Record prints 'IN PROGRESS — 3 of 6 items reviewed', then 'Reviewed and accepted as the record …' and Robert Hale's signature line. The sign-off is withheld only while a line has no disposition (havellin.html:34500-34505).

findings.title: Trust-only packages still call the papers and folders 'Estate Inventory' and 'the estate's Drive folder'
findings.where: printEstateInventoryReport title and the 'estate's Drive folder' sentence, _pkgShareFolders label 'Estate Inventory photographs', PROBATE_PKG_TITLES.schedule
findings.evidence: a4.js trust package email: attachments 'Trust Schedule' and 'Estate Inventory Report', the link 'Estate Inventory photographs'. trust_report.html: 'Estate Inventory — Asset Schedule … filed in the estate's Drive folder', on a matter whose party head is 'The Price Family Trust'. P19 renamed the snapshot for exactly this reason.
findings.tc_impact: A successor trustee's counsel reads estate wording on a trust administration, a small but noticeable slip in a market where most homes are in trust.
findings.proposal: On a matter where matterDef(job).trust holds and onProbate does not, title the Report 'Inventory — Asset Schedule' and use 'the trust's Drive folder' and 'Inventory photographs'. The folder name in Drive need not change.
findings.vnote: On the trust matter (party head 'The Price Family Trust (Estate of Walter Price)'), the Report's h2 is 'Estate Inventory — Asset Schedule', and its no-photo note says 'filed in the estate’s Drive folder'. The package's folder label is 'Estate Inventory photographs' (havellin.html:17988). The email itself does say 'the trust’s Google Drive folder'.
